//: Composite indexes required by the admin queries.
Firestore needs a composite index when a query combines a filter with an
ordering on a different field, or with an inequality. The emulator does NOT
enforce this — it serves such queries happily — so a missing entry here
fails only in production, with 'The query requires an index'.
It does NOT need one for several equality filters together: Firestore
answers those by intersecting the automatic single-field indexes. This was
measured against the live project rather than assumed, which is why the two
`products` entries that used to be listed here are gone — isActive +
isFeatured and isActive + categoryKey both work without them, and an index
that earns nothing still costs storage and write latency.
Deploy with: npm run rules:deploy
The storefront catalogue queries deliberately avoid needing indexes: they
filter on equality only and sort in memory, because the catalogue is small
and an index that only exists in production is a trap.

indexes.//: listOrders() filtered by status — where status == X, orderBy createdAt desc

//: getDashboardStats() revenue — where paymentStatus == PAID and
status != CANCELLED, aggregating sum(totalCents).
`totalCents` is in the index because it is SUMMED, not filtered. A
sum() or avg() can only be served by an index that contains the
aggregated field, and Firestore rejects the query outright otherwise.
Nothing about the filters hints at this, and the emulator runs the
query happily either way — it was found by the live project refusing
it. Removing totalCents here breaks the admin dashboard in production
only.
